summary: Boot-persistent Windows service turns installer host into a remotely-driven AI shell executor
details: On Windows, the postinstall script registers a boot-persistent auto-restart Windows service (via node-windows and sc.exe start=auto with failure reset) that launches service/daemon.js and service/worker.js at boot. The daemon runs `npm install -g opencode-ai@latest` (unpinned) and spawns `opencode serve --port 4096` as a local AI-agent execution backend. worker.js connects to a hardcoded RongCloud IM tenant at https://newsradar.dreamdt.cn (AppKey bmdehs6pbyyks), subscribes to inbound chat messages, and forwards each message as a prompt to the local opencode agent, whose system prompt directs it to execute shell/ops commands (pkill, nohup, systemctl, config edits, backups) on the host. Network-sourced messages from a publisher-controlled channel are thus dispatched as executable commands on the installer's machine. In addition, service/updater.js polls every six hours from the same boot-persistent service and, on any version bump, runs `npm install -g claw-subagent-service@<latest>` and restarts the worker with the new code, converting a single install into a permanent code-push channel controlled by the publisher.
